battle.name: 西班牙內戰
battle.brief: 西班牙內戰在1936年7月爆發後，共和派與國民軍在馬德里、巴塞隆納、格蘭納達等城市以及北部山區形成激烈的前線。蘇聯提供的T-26輕型坦克在共和軍的機械化單位中被部署，用以支援步兵突破並在城市防守中提供有限的裝甲火力。

kit.name: T-26輕型坦克
kit.history: 作為共和軍的主力輕型坦克，T-26在西班牙內戰中於城市防守與機動支援中提供裝甲火力。

countries: 西班牙內戰的根本陣營分為兩大對立陣營：一方為第二共和國政府及其支持的左翼政黨、工會與武裝民兵，稱為共和派；另一方為以弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥為首的國民軍（亦稱民族派），結合了傳統軍官、保守派貴族、教會勢力以及極端的法西斯黨派——法西斯主義的長槍黨與卡洛斯派的卡洛斯主義者。戰爭期間，外國勢力的介入極大地塑造了雙方的軍事格局。納粹德國與法西斯意大利向國民軍提供了大量的機械化裝備、空軍與軍事顧問，並組織了「秃鷹軍團」在西班牙作戰；葡萄牙的萨拉查政權亦提供了物資與志願兵。另一方面，蘇聯與墨西哥則向共和派輸送了戰鬥機、坦克、火炮及軍事顧問，並在國際縱隊的名義下召集了來自法國、英國、美國、德國、波蘭等國的志願者加入前線。
countriesEn: The fundamental camps of the Spanish Civil War were divided into two major opposing sides: on one side stood the Second Republic government and its leftist parties, unions and armed militia, collectively referred to as the Republicans; on the other side were the Nationalist insurgents led by Francisco Franco, combining traditional officers, conservative aristocracy, church forces and the extreme fascist Falange and the Carlist carlists. During the war, foreign interventions greatly shaped the military configuration of both sides. Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy supplied the Nationalists with large quantities of mechanised equipment, air support and military advisors, and organized the Condor Legion to fight in Spain; Portugal's Salazar regime also provided materiel and volunteers. On the other side, the Soviet Union and Mexico delivered fighters, tanks, artillery and military advisors to the Republicans, and under the banner of the International Brigades recruited volunteers from France, Britain, the United States, Germany, Poland and other countries to join the front lines.
people: 在這場武裝衝突中，雙方均有眾多具有代表性的軍事與政治領袖。國民軍方面，弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥元帥於1936年9月被任命為最高統帥，指揮非洲軍團以及後續的北上進攻；何塞·莫斯卡多將軍率領特種步兵營，負責保衛重要的港口城市；胡安·亞格將軍以其在西班牙外籍軍團的作戰經驗，指揮快速突破的機械化縱隊；岡薩洛·克波·德·利亞諾在塞維利亞的廣播宣傳與軍事行動中扮演關鍵角色。共和派方面，荷西·米亞哈將軍在馬德里防禦戰中成為核心指揮官，率領正規軍與武裝群眾共同抵禦包圍；共產黨領袖多洛雷斯·伊巴露麗以其激昂的演說激勵前線士兵；無政府主義領袖布埃娜文圖拉·杜羅提與弗朗西斯科·阿斯卡西則率領武裝工人游擊隊在城市與鄉村展開游擊戰；國際縱隊的軍事顧問如安德烈·馬蒂（法國）與沃爾特·馮·托馬（德國）亦在戰術策劃上提供寶貴經驗。
peopleEn: On both sides of the armed conflict there were many representative military and political leaders. Among the Nationalists, Field Marshal Francisco Franco was appointed Supreme Commander in September 1936 and directed the Army of Africa and the subsequent north‑ward offensive; General José Moscardó led special infantry battalions guarding key port cities; General Juan Yagüe, drawing on his experience with the Spanish Legion, commanded rapid‑moving mechanised columns; General Gonzalo Queipo de Llano played a crucial role in both the radio propaganda and military operations in Seville. On the Republican side, General José Miaja became the core commander during the defense of Madrid, leading regular troops and armed civilians together; Communist leader Dolores Ibárruri inspired frontline soldiers with her impassioned speeches; anarchist leaders Buenaventura Durruti and Francisco Ascaso headed armed worker guerrillas fighting in cities and countryside; International Brigades' military advisors such as André Marty of France and Walter von Thoma of Germany also contributed valuable experience to tactical planning.
kits: 裝備方面，交戰雙方使用的武器與車輛均屬1930年代中期已列裝的真實型號。國民軍的步兵主要配備德國製造的毛瑟98步槍（口徑7.92×57mm），機槍則包括MG 13與MG 08/15，口徑同為7.92mm；火力支援依賴於10.5 cm leIG 18步兵炮與15 cm sIG 33重型步兵炮；坦克部隊則裝甲了德國的Panzer I A型（裝甲厚度13mm）與Panzer II（武裝20mm機炮），以及義大利的CV-33裝甲車；空軍方面，國民軍使用Heinkel He 51戰鬥機、Fiat CR.32與Ju 52轟炸機，並在1937年引入Messerschmitt Bf 109（初期為Bf 109B）。共和派的武器則以蘇聯提供的主力裝備為主：步槍使用7.62×54mm的莫辛-納干步槍；機槍包括DP-27輕機槍與M1910馬克沁重機槍；火炮則配備76.2 mm F-22野戰炮與122 mm howitzer；坦克則裝甲了蘇聯T-26（口徑45mm炮）與BT-5快速坦克；空軍則使用Polikarpov I-16單翼戰鬥機與Polikarpov R-5偵察機，並接受了少量義大利製的Saia-Marchetti SM.79轟炸機。所有武器與車輛均已在1936年前列裝，確保了雙方在技術層面的真實可比性。
kitsEn: In terms of equipment, the weapons and vehicles used by both combatants were real models that had entered service in the mid‑1930s. Nationalist infantry were principally equipped with the German Mauser 98 rifle (7.92×57 mm), while machine guns included the MG 13 and the MG 08/15, also chambered for 7.92 mm; fire support relied on the 10.5 cm leIG 18 infantry gun and the 15 cm sIG 33 heavy infantry gun; tank units were armored with German Panzer I Ausf. A (13 mm armor) and Panzer II (armed with a 20 mm cannon), as well as Italian CV‑33 armored cars; in the air, the Nationalists flew Heinkel He 51 fighters, Fiat CR.32 fighters and Ju 52 bombers, and began receiving Messerschmitt Bf 109 (initially the Bf 109B) in 1937. Republican weapons were mainly supplied by the Soviet Union: rifles were the 7.62×54 mm Mosin‑Nagant; machine guns comprised the DP‑27 light machine gun and the M1910 Maxim heavy machine gun; artillery included the 76.2 mm F‑22 field gun and 122 mm howitzers; tanks were the Soviet T‑26 (equipped with a 45 mm gun) and BT‑5 fast tanks; the air force used the Polikarpov I‑16 monoplane fighter and the Polikarpov R‑5 reconnaissance aircraft, and received a limited number of Italian‑built Savoia‑Marchetti SM.79 bombers. All weapons and vehicles had been listed in service before 1936, ensuring genuine comparability between the two sides.
tactics: 在戰術層面，國民軍採用了以機械化縱隊為核心的快速突破與分割包圍戰術。1936年9月，佛朗哥率領非洲軍團從摩洛哥北上，結合德國Panzer I與義大利CV-33裝甲車，在托萊多與埃斯特雷馬杜拉之間形成快速穿插線；同時，德國空軍的Heinkel He 51與Ju 52提供近距離空中支援，壓制共和派的防線。國民軍的炮兵則以10.5 cm leIG 18與15 cm sIG 33在步兵衝擊前進行地毯式轟炸，以削弱防守陣地。相較之下，共和派最初依賴游擊式的武裝群眾與城市守備隊，採用分散的小股兵力在街巷、工廠與山區構築防禦工事；在馬德里保衛戰中，共和軍在市區部署了由志願兵組成的「人民兵團」，以街壘、手榴彈與DP-27機槍抵禦國民軍的坦克。隨著戰爭的推進，共和派在1937年接受了蘇聯顧問的正規化改造，將原有的民兵整編為步兵師與炮兵團，開始實行正規的防線構築與集中的火力支援，並在巴塞羅那與華倫西亞建立持久的後勤供應線。此後，雙方在布列塔尼（Berlín）與埃布羅河的攻防中，展示了陣地戰與渡河戰的典型模式。
tacticsEn: At the tactical level, the Nationalists employed a rapid‑breakthrough and encirclement doctrine centred on mechanised columns. In September 1936, Franco led the Army of Africa northwards from Morocco, combining German Panzer I and Italian CV‑33 armoured cars to create fast‑moving thrusts between Toledo and Extremadura, while German Luftwaffe He 51 and Ju 52 aircraft provided close‑air support to suppress Republican positions. Nationalist artillery, using the 10.5 cm leIG 18 and 15 cm sIG 33, delivered carpet‑type bombardments ahead of infantry assaults to weaken defensive positions. By contrast, the Republicans initially relied on guerrilla‑style armed civilians and urban defense units, deploying small, dispersed forces to build barricades in streets, factories and mountainous terrain. During the defence of Madrid, Republican troops formed “people’s militia” units that fought with hand‑grenades, DP‑27 machine guns and improvised explosives to repulse Nationalist tanks. As the war progressed, the Republicans, advised by Soviet specialists, reorganised their militia into regular infantry divisions and artillery regiments, adopting conventional trench construction and concentrated fire support, and established sustained supply lines around Barcelona and Valencia. Subsequently, both sides demonstrated classic positional warfare and river‑crossing tactics in the battles of the Brunete salient and the Ebro River.
data: 根據現有的歷史統計，戰爭開始時國民軍在非洲集結約80,000至100,000名士兵，加上在本土的起義軍，總兵力約在150,000人左右；共和派的武裝力量在同時期約有200,000名志願民兵與正規軍。隨著1937年的大規模動員，雙方兵力均膨脹至接近100萬人，形成了大規模的正面交戰與持久消耗的局面。主要戰役時間表如下：1936年7月18日至20日的武裝起義與摩洛哥的起義；1936年8月托萊多與巴塞羅那的激烈巷戰；1936年9月佛朗哥被任命為最高統帥；1936年11月8日馬德里保衛戰正式展開，直至1939年3月28日馬德里陷落；1937年2月的雅拉馬河戰役；1937年3月的瓜達拉哈拉會戰；1937年4月26日的格蘭尼卡轟炸；1937年7月的布朗內特攻勢；1937年9月的貝爾奇特鎮爭奪；1938年7月至11月的埃布羅河大反攻；以及1939年3月的最終突破與投降。傷亡方面，根據多數史學家的估算，整體死亡人數在30萬至50萬人之間，其中包括大量的軍事人員與因戰鬥導致的間接死亡。
dataEn: According to existing historical statistics, at the outbreak of the war the Nationalists had assembled roughly 80,000‑100,000 men in Africa, together with insurgents on the peninsula, bringing their total to about 150,000 troops; the Republican armed forces at the same time comprised about 200,000 volunteer militiamen and regular soldiers. With the massive mobilisations of 1937, both sides expanded to close to one million men, resulting in large‑scale frontal engagements and prolonged attrition. The principal chronological milestones are as follows: the military uprisings of 17‑20 July 1936 in Morocco, Cadiz, Seville and Zaragoza; intense street fighting in Toledo and Barcelona in August 1936; Franco’s appointment as Supreme Commander in September 1936; the formal commencement of the Siege of Madrid on 8 November 1936, lasting until the city fell on 28 March 1939; the Battle of the Jarama River in February 1937; the Battle of Guadalajara in March 1937; the bombing of Guernica on 26 April 1937; the Republican offensive at Brunete in July 1937; the struggle for Belchite in September 1937; the large‑scale Ebro counter‑offensive from July to November 1938; and the final breakthrough and surrender in March 1939. In terms of casualties, most historians estimate total deaths in the range of 300,000‑500,000, a figure that includes a large proportion of military personnel and indirect losses caused by combat.
cause: 西班牙內戰的起因根植於1930年代初期的政治與社會危機。1931年宣布成立的第二共和國推行土地改革、教育的世俗化以及軍隊的去政治化等措施，引發了保守派與教會勢力的激烈反對；經濟大蕭條導致農業與工業產出大幅下降，失業率飆升，城鄉矛盾加劇。左翼政黨如共產黨與無政府主義的西班牙工人階級聯盟（CNT-FAI）組織罷工與武裝暴動；右翼方面，以长枪党為代表的法西斯組織與傳統軍官階層在軍隊內部形成祕密同盟，計畫以軍事政變推翻共和國。1936年2月的議會選舉中，人民陣線以微弱多數勝出，隨即展開激進的改革與對軍隊的清洗，刺激了軍官們的叛亂決心。軍官們以保護西班牙「傳統價值」與「國家統一」為口號，於1936年7月17日至18日在摩洛哥、加的斯、塞維利亞與薩拉戈薩等地發動叛亂，標誌著內戰的正式爆發。外國法西斯政權對叛亂者提供軍事援助，使得衝突迅速升級為代理戰爭。
causeEn: The origins of the Spanish Civil War lay in the political and social crisis of the early 1930s. The Second Republic, proclaimed in 1931, introduced agrarian reform, the secularisation of education and the depoliticisation of the army, provoking fierce opposition from conservative and ecclesiastical circles; the Great Depression caused a dramatic fall in agricultural and industrial output, soaring unemployment and heightened urban‑rural tensions. Left‑wing parties such as the Communist Party and the anarchist CNT‑FAI organized strikes and armed uprisings, while on the right the Falange and traditional officer corps forged a secret alliance within the army, planning a coup to overthrow the Republic. In the February 1936 parliamentary elections, the Popular Front won a narrow majority and promptly launched radical reforms together with a purge of the armed forces, spurring the conspirators’ resolve to rebel. Officers proclaimed the defence of Spain’s “traditional values” and “national unity,” and on 17‑18 July 1936 launched uprisings in Morocco, Cadiz, Seville, Zaragoza and other cities, marking the formal outbreak of civil war. Foreign fascist regimes provided military aid to the rebels, turning the conflict into a proxy war.
impact: 內戰對西班牙及其國際格局留下了深遠的影響。首先，戰爭造成了巨大的人員傷亡與物質破壞，估計死亡人數在30萬至50萬之間，導致大批知識分子、藝術家與科學家流亡至法國、墨西哥與蘇聯，其中不少人在 exile 中繼續從事反法西斯與文化創作，對後世的西班牙文學與藝術產生深遠影響。其次，佛朗哥在戰後建立了以個人崇拜為核心的獨裁政權，實施長期的政治迫害與新聞檢查，壓制一切反對聲音，並在二戰期間與軸心國保持有限度的合作，維持西班牙的中立直到戰後。再次，戰爭成為歐洲各國政治立場的試金石，德國與意大利利用西班牙內戰測試新式武器與戰術，如坦克與空中轟炸；而蘇聯則借此機會向共產國際展示其軍事與意識形態輸出能力。西班牙內戰還催生了大量的戰爭文學與藝術作品，特別是巴勃羅·畢加索的油畫《格蘭尼卡》成為反戰的象徵，並在國際社會引發了對法西斯主義的道德譴責。最後，內戰的結果預示了二戰期間游擊戰與城市游擊戰的戰略演變，並對後續的冷戰格局產生影響，因為西班牙的獨裁體制成為西方陣營在意識形態上的一個缺口。
impactEn: The civil war left a profound imprint on Spain and the international scene. First, it caused enormous loss of life and material destruction, with death tolls estimated between 300,000 and 500,000, and forced a massive exile of intellectuals, artists and scientists to France, Mexico and the Soviet Union, many of whom continued anti‑fascist work and cultural production abroad, deeply influencing post‑war Spanish literature and art. Secondly, Franco established a personal‑cult dictatorship after the war, imposing long‑term political persecution, press censorship and the suppression of all opposition, and during World War II maintained limited cooperation with the Axis powers while keeping Spain neutral until the post‑war period. The war also served as a testing ground for European powers: Germany and Italy used it to field‑test new weapons and tactics such as tanks and strategic bombing, while the Soviet Union showcased its military and ideological export capability to the Comintern. The conflict generated a wealth of war literature and art, notably Pablo Picasso’s mural “Guernica,” which became an anti‑war symbol and provoked international moral condemnation of fascism. Finally, the Spanish conflict foreshadowed the guerrilla and urban warfare strategies of World War II and influenced the Cold‑War balance, as Spain’s dictatorship became an ideological gap in the Western camp that the United States and Western Europe later embraced in the anti‑Soviet strategy.
result: 最終，國民軍於1939年3月28日攻陷馬德里，標誌著西班牙內戰的正式結束，佛朗哥隨即成立「國防委員會」與「臨時政府」，將所有政黨解散，並以「單一黨」长枪党為唯一合法政治組織，建立起持續至1975年的長達三十六年之久的法西斯獨裁政權。戰後的西班牙在政治上實行了嚴厲的清洗與鎮壓，數以千計的前共和派官員、軍人與知識分子被處決或監禁，經濟則在國家干預與自給自足的政策下逐步恢復，但伴隨著長期的生活水平低點與國際孤立。外交上，佛朗哥在二戰初期保持「非交戰」立場，與軸心國保持有限的經濟與軍事往來，卻未正式加入軸心國，從而在戰後得以在國際社會中維持一定的生存空間。1945年後，隨著冷戰的加劇，美國與西歐國家對西班牙的獨裁政權逐漸轉變為「遏制蘇聯」戰略中的盟友，提供了經濟援助與軍事合作，進一步延長了佛朗哥政權的存續。直至1975年佛朗哥逝世，西班牙在過渡時期實行了民主改革，建立了君主立憲制，結束了長期的專制統治。整體而言，西班牙內戰的結果不僅決定了西班牙的政治走向，也深刻影響了20世紀歐洲的法西斯主義、共產主義與民主運動之間的力量對比。
resultEn: In the end, the Nationalists captured Madrid on 28 March 1939, marking the official conclusion of the Spanish Civil War. Franco immediately formed a “Junta de Defensa” and a “provisional government,” dissolved all political parties, and, with the Falange as the sole legal party, established a fascist dictatorship that lasted until his death in 1975, a span of thirty‑six years. The post‑war period was characterised by severe purges and repression: thousands of former Republican officials, soldiers and intellectuals were executed or imprisoned, while the economy was rebuilt under state‑directed autarkic policies, resulting in prolonged low living standards and international isolation. Diplomatic‑ly, Franco initially kept Spain “non‑belligerent” during World War II, maintaining limited economic and military contacts with the Axis yet refraining from formal entry, which allowed the regime to survive the post‑war years. After 1945, as the Cold War intensified, the United States and Western European nations shifted their stance, viewing Spain as a useful ally against the Soviet Union and providing economic aid and military cooperation, further extending the regime’s lifespan. Only after Franco’s death in 1975 did Spain undergo a democratic transition, establishing a constitutional monarchy and ending decades of authoritarian rule. In sum, the outcome of the Spanish Civil War determined Spain’s political trajectory and profoundly reshaped the balance between fascism, communism and democracy in 20th‑century Europe.
